beginner: rule of thirds and basic framing vocabulary
understands value as lightness independent of hue
working_professional: controls focal hierarchy through value contrast, not just placement
designs compositions that read at thumbnail, mid-distance, and full size
builds color relationships from temperature, saturation, and value
produces controlled value keys: high-key, low-key, full-range
senior: diagnoses why a composition fails despite correct rule application
recognizes value-grouping failures from local contrast conflicts
understands color as structural hierarchy tool, not decoration
critiques saturation exhaustion and weak focal budgeting
lead_director: establishes composition/value/color canon that scales across media
knows when a color script is ready for production
rejects technically-correct but visually-dead compositions with causal reasoning

composition_principles.definition: One dominant point. Hierarchy via contrast (value, color, scale, detail, isolation).
composition_principles.failure: everything-shouts: competing focal points with equal contrast

composition_principles.definition: Shapes with similar value read as one group. If 3-value thumbnail fails, composition fails.
composition_principles.failure: value-bleed: adjacent shapes share same value

composition_principles.definition: Space around subjects carries structural weight equal to subjects.
Repeated/varied spacing creates visual beat guiding scanning.
Relative size determines perceived importance. Scale contrast is strongest hierarchy tool.
Hard edges draw eye; soft edges recede; lost edges invite depth.
Overlap, scale diminution, atmospheric perspective, value falloff, temperature shift signal depth.

value_principles.definition: Value carries more structural weight than color. Works in grayscale = works in color.
value_principles.failure: color-dependent-structure: relies on hue for hierarchy

value_principles.definition: Max contrast is finite resource. Spend at focal point.
High-key, low-key, full-range create different emotional registers.
Midtones carry readable detail. Crushed blacks/blown whites destroy information.

color_principles.definition: Warm advances, cool recedes. Temperature defines spatial depth more reliably than hue.
High saturation demands attention. Gray is context that makes color meaningful.
Color changes with surroundings. Design relationships, not isolated swatches.
Color encodes categories but must never be sole information channel.
color_principles.failure: color-only-coding: critical info via hue alone

color_principles.definition: 3-7 colors with clear roles produce stronger identity than unlimited choice.
color_principles.failure: palette-bloat: dozens of colors, no role structure

failure_patterns.repair: restore midtone separation with motivated fill
assign dominant focal, reduce contrast elsewhere
reduce 80% to low-medium, reserve high for focal

why_is_my_composition_flat: Is there one dominant focal point with maximum contrast?
Are secondary areas demonstrably lower contrast?
Do you have clear foreground/midground/background value plan?
Are there rest areas for the eye?
why_does_my_color_feel_chaotic: Is there a clear temperature strategy?
Does the palette have assigned roles?
Have you tested adjacency effects between key pairs?

micro_labs.goal: Readable composition with exactly 3 values before color/detail
micro_labs.success: reads at postage-stamp size, focal clear

micro_labs.goal: Composition with exactly 5 colors and clear role assignment
micro_labs.success: every color role identifiable, palette intentional

micro_labs.goal: Convert color composition to grayscale, diagnose value-grouping failures
Map contrast budget: highest/medium/lowest regions vs intended hierarchy

transfer_tests.goal: Apply value/color principles from character to environment/UI
Re-block high-key composition in low-key without losing hierarchy

golden_tasks.description: Analyze composition: focal hierarchy, value structure, color relationships, 2+ failure patterns with causal diagnosis
Given black-crush or value-bleed failures, produce repaired version
Critique palette: saturation, temperature, roles, accessibility

cross_pack_links.relationship: Structural foundation that art direction orchestrates, typography inhabits, motion activates

known_limits: No script can certify visual taste or emotional impact.
Color perception is physiological and cultural.
Provides professional vocabulary and diagnostic frameworks, not automated scoring.
provenance_note: Authored from model knowledge. Requires KAPIF research evidence before canon eligibility.
